location: No step fails. I checked the whole argument (Steps 0–3 and the Conclusion).
objection:
I found no gap. Checks made:
(1) Factorisation. For squarefree t = t1 t2 t3, gcd(t^2, q) = t2 t3^2. So m_t(q) = t1^2 t2, x/(q m_t(q)) = Z/t1^2 with Z = x/(q t2), and eta(t) m_t(q) = eta(t2) eta(t3) t2 kappa(t1). All correct.
(2) Regrouping is justified by absolute convergence. Each term is at most eta(t) x/q, and the sum of eta(t) is finite.
(3) P5(c) is used exactly as stated: the coprimality condition (t1, q) = 1 matches, it holds for every q in N and real Z > 0, and the constant is c(eps) q^eps.
(4) Error term: q^{1+eps} (x/q)^{1/3} t2^{2/3} = x^{1/3} q^{2/3+eps} t2^{2/3}. The sums of eta(t2) t2^{2/3} and of eta(t3) are bounded by absolute Euler products, using eta(t) <= 2^{omega(t)} t^{-2}.
(5) Main term: q t2 sqrt(Z) = sqrt(xq) t2^{1/2}. I verified all three local-factor identities: (p-1)^2(p+2)/p^3 = 1 - 3/p^2 + 2/p^3; (p-1)(p^2-2+sqrt p)/p^3; and (p-1)^2(p+1)/p^3. Their product times I is exactly h(q).
(6) Uniformity: the constant is C1 C2 c(eps), which depends only on eps. The bound holds for every x > 0 and q >= 1, so in particular on the stated range 1 <= q <= x. No result from 2011 or later is cited; only P5 is used.
Numerical check: I computed MT with t <= 4·10^5 against h(q) sqrt(xq). The differences were -0.6, 1.4, 16.9, 24.6, -68.7 and -851, for (x, q) = (1e6, 1), (1e6, 12), (1e6, 72), (1e7, 360), (1e8, 4), (1e8, 1000). Each is well below x^{1/3} q^{2/3}, and part of it is the truncation tail of order x/(qN).
other_issues: Cosmetic: the 'Numerical sanity check' section reports a difference of 92 at (x, q) = (10^6, 1). That figure comes from truncating at t <= 3000, which leaves a tail of order A0·x/3000. With a larger cutoff (t <= 4·10^5) the difference is about -0.6. This section is not used in the proof.
